This notebook completes both parts of the QBIO 490 Week 7 transcriptomics exercise. Run on CARC with access to the existing TCGA-BRCA GDC download. Numerical answers are printed from the actual dataset rather than assumed.

## Part 1 — TCGA RNA-seq data

### Setup and packages

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
analysis_dir <- "/home1/puyuanli/490_cluster/analysis_data"
if (!dir.exists(analysis_dir)) stop("Missing analysis_data directory: ", analysis_dir)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(analysis_dir))
setwd(analysis_dir)  # Also set the working directory for interactive RStudio execution
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
```

```{r packages}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly=TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
required_bioc <- c("TCGAbiolinks", "SummarizedExperiment", "DESeq2", "EnhancedVolcano")
missing_bioc <- required_bioc[!vapply(required_bioc, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly=TRUE)]
if (length(missing_bioc)) BiocManager::install(missing_bioc, ask=FALSE, update=FALSE)
library(TCGAbiolinks)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(DESeq2)
library(EnhancedVolcano)
```

### Load RNA-seq data

The earlier Materials Download assignment downloaded TCGA-BRCA STAR counts. `GDCprepare()` uses the existing local download when it is present. If it reports missing files, uncomment `GDCdownload(rna_query)` and run it once before `GDCprepare()`.

```{r load-rna}
rna_query <- GDCquery(project="TCGA-BRCA",
                      data.category="Transcriptome Profiling",
                      data.type="Gene Expression Quantification",
                      workflow.type="STAR - Counts")
# GDCdownload(rna_query)  # ONLY if the required local GDC files are missing
rna_se <- GDCprepare(rna_query)
stopifnot(inherits(rna_se, "SummarizedExperiment"))
```


### Exercise 1.3 — What do the rows and columns represent?

- **colData:** rows represent sequenced samples (identified by sample barcodes); columns represent clinical and sample metadata variables.
- **rowRanges elementMetadata:** rows represent genes/features; columns describe gene annotations, such as gene IDs and names.
- **unstranded assay:** rows represent the same genes/features as rowRanges; columns represent the same samples, in the same order, as colData. Entries are raw read counts.

```{r exercise-1-3}
head(rownames(colData(rna_se))); colnames(colData(rna_se))
head(rownames(mcols(rowRanges(rna_se)))); colnames(mcols(rowRanges(rna_se)))
head(rownames(assay(rna_se, "unstranded"))); head(colnames(assay(rna_se, "unstranded")))
stopifnot(nrow(colData(rna_se)) == ncol(rna_se),
          nrow(mcols(rowRanges(rna_se))) == nrow(rna_se))
```

### Exercises 2.3–2.6 — Clinical data cleaning

```{r exercise-2-3-to-2-6}
rna_clinical <- as.data.frame(colData(rna_se))
columns_to_remove <- c("treatments", "primary_site", "disease_type", "sites_of_involvement")
rna_clinical <- rna_clinical[, !(names(rna_clinical) %in% columns_to_remove), drop=FALSE]
# Save the sample-level mask before filtering so it can also subset assay columns.
age_numeric <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(rna_clinical$age_at_index)))
age_NA_mask <- !is.na(age_numeric)
rna_clinical <- rna_clinical[age_NA_mask, , drop=FALSE]
rna_clinical$age_at_index <- age_numeric[age_NA_mask]
summary(rna_clinical$age_at_index)
stopifnot(!anyNA(rna_clinical$age_at_index))
```

### Exercises 5.1 and 5.4 — Clinical identifiers and age categories

Patients aged **58 or younger** are categorized as `young`; those **older than 58** as `old`.

```{r exercise-5-1-and-5-4}
head(rownames(rna_clinical)); colnames(rna_clinical)
rna_clinical$age_category <- ifelse(rna_clinical$age_at_index <= 58, "young", "old")
rna_clinical$age_category <- factor(rna_clinical$age_category, levels=c("young", "old"))
table(rna_clinical$age_category, useNA="ifany")
```

### Exercises 5.5–5.6 — Gene identifiers

Gene IDs are used as row names because gene names are not necessarily unique. Do **not** execute the duplicate-prone `rownames(rna_genes) <- rna_genes$gene_name` assignment.

```{r exercise-5-5-to-5-6}
head(rownames(rna_genes)); colnames(rna_genes)
stopifnot("gene_id" %in% colnames(rna_genes), !anyNA(rna_genes$gene_id),

rownames(rna_genes) <- as.character(rna_genes$gene_id)
head(rownames(rna_genes))
```

## Part 2 — Differential expression analysis

### Exercise 1 — Read the saved tables

```{r part2-exercise-1}
rna_clinical <- read.csv(file.path(analysis_dir, "brca_rna_clinical_data.csv"), row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
rna_genes <- read.csv(file.path(analysis_dir, "brca_rna_gene_data.csv"), check.names=FALSE)
rna_counts <- read.csv(file.path(analysis_dir, "brca_rna_count_data.csv"), row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(rna_counts), rownames(rna_clinical)))
```

### Exercise 2 — Prepare sample covariate and filter genes

The requested comparison is **Tumor versus Normal**. Age is the chosen covariate; it is converted to numeric years and included in the design. PAM50 is not used because subtype is often unavailable or biologically undefined for normal samples. The analysis therefore estimates the tumor/normal effect while adjusting for age.

```{r part2-exercise-2}
stopifnot("definition" %in% names(rna_clinical), "age_at_index" %in% names(rna_clinical))
rna_clinical$age_at_index <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(rna_clinical$age_at_index)))
print(table(rna_clinical$definition, useNA="ifany"))
# TCGA typically labels these groups "Primary solid Tumor" and "Solid Tissue Normal".
# Check the displayed labels rather than assuming all datasets use identical capitalization.
definition_text <- tolower(trimws(as.character(rna_clinical$definition)))
is_normal <- grepl("normal", definition_text)
is_tumor <- grepl("tumou?r", definition_text) & !is_normal
keep_samples <- (is_normal | is_tumor) & !is.na(rna_clinical$age_at_index)
rna_clinical <- rna_clinical[keep_samples, , drop=FALSE]
rna_counts <- rna_counts[, keep_samples, drop=FALSE]
rna_clinical$definition_group <- factor(ifelse(is_tumor[keep_samples], "Tumor", "Normal"),
                                        levels=c("Normal", "Tumor"))
stopifnot(identical(colnames(rna_counts), rownames(rna_clinical)),
          all(c("Normal", "Tumor") %in% rna_clinical$definition_group),
          !anyNA(rna_clinical$age_at_index), !anyNA(rna_clinical$definition_group))
print(table(rna_clinical$definition_group))
# DESeq2 requires nonnegative integer raw counts.
counts_matrix <- as.matrix(rna_counts)
stopifnot(is.numeric(counts_matrix), all(is.finite(counts_matrix)),
          all(counts_matrix >= 0), all(counts_matrix == round(counts_matrix)))
keep_genes <- rowSums(counts_matrix) >= 1000
counts_matrix <- counts_matrix[keep_genes, , drop=FALSE]
cat("Genes retained (total count >= 1000):", nrow(counts_matrix), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(counts_matrix)>0)
```

### Exercise 3 — Run DESeq2 and save results

Design: `~ age_at_index + definition_group`. The `Tumor`/`Normal` contrast is explicitly ordered so that **positive log2 fold changes indicate higher expression in tumor samples** and negative values indicate higher expression in normal samples.

```{r part2-exercise-3}
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData=counts_matrix,
                              colData=rna_clinical,
                              design=~ age_at_index + definition_group)
dds_obj <- DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds_obj)
results <- DESeq2::results(dds_obj, format="DataFrame",
                           contrast=c("definition_group", "Tumor", "Normal"))
results <- as.data.frame(results)
write.csv(results, file.path(analysis_dir, "brca_DESeq_results.csv"), row.names=TRUE)
saveRDS(results, file.path(analysis_dir, "brca_DESeq_results.rds"))
summary(DESeq2::results(dds_obj, contrast=c("definition_group", "Tumor", "Normal")))
```

### Prepare gene labels for EnhancedVolcano

Match gene IDs in the DESeq2 result rows to `rna_genes$gene_id`, rather than relying on row positions after filtering.

```{r part2-gene-labels}
stopifnot(all(c("gene_id", "gene_name") %in% names(rna_genes)))
match_idx <- match(rownames(results), as.character(rna_genes$gene_id))
stopifnot(!anyNA(match_idx))
results$gene_name <- as.character(rna_genes$gene_name[match_idx])
missing_labels <- is.na(results$gene_name) | results$gene_name == ""
results$gene_name[missing_labels] <- rownames(results)[missing_labels]
head(results[, c("log2FoldChange", "pvalue", "padj", "gene_name")])
# Update the saved results to include gene_name as requested for plotting and reuse.
write.csv(results, file.path(analysis_dir, "brca_DESeq_results.csv"), row.names=TRUE)
saveRDS(results, file.path(analysis_dir, "brca_DESeq_results.rds"))
```

### Exercise 4 — EnhancedVolcano plot

```{r part2-exercise-4, fig.width=11, fig.height=8}
volcano <- EnhancedVolcano(results,
                           lab=results$gene_name,
                           x="log2FoldChange",
                           y="padj",
                           title="Sample Definition: Tumor vs Normal Tissue",
                           pointSize=1.0,
                           labSize=5.0)
print(volcano)
figure_path <- "/home1/puyuanli/490_cluster/week7_transcriptomics/brca_tumor_vs_normal_volcano.png"
dir.create(dirname(figure_path), recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(filename=figure_path, plot=volcano, width=11, height=8, dpi=300)
cat("Saved volcano plot:", figure_path, "\n")
```

### Exercise 5 — Interpret the six regions of the volcano plot

The x-axis is log2(Tumor / Normal) fold change; the y-axis is −log10(adjusted p-value). Higher positions indicate stronger statistical significance. The plot uses EnhancedVolcano's default significance thresholds unless explicitly changed.

- **Top-right:** genes with higher expression in tumors (positive log2 fold change) and statistically significant adjusted p-values; strong candidates for tumor-upregulated genes. Those past both thresholds are highlighted as meeting both criteria.
- **Bottom-right:** genes with higher estimated expression in tumors but weak statistical evidence (larger adjusted p-values); cannot confidently call them differentially expressed.
- **Top-left:** genes with lower expression in tumors (negative log2 fold change; relatively higher in normal tissue) and statistically significant adjusted p-values; candidates for tumor-downregulated genes.
- **Bottom-left:** genes with lower estimated expression in tumors but insufficient statistical evidence for differential expression.
- **Top-middle:** genes with small estimated fold changes near zero but potentially statistically significant adjusted p-values. A statistically significant change need not be large in magnitude.
- **Bottom-middle:** genes with fold changes near zero and non-significant adjusted p-values; no convincing evidence of differential expression.

Note that a gene's horizontal position alone does not establish significance, and a high position alone does not establish a large effect size. Genes with missing adjusted p-values cannot be interpreted as significant.
